# Quick Design Spec: Repair Cost

**Classification:** Tuning — change a number without adding a new state.
**GDD Reference:** design/gdd/repair.md

## Change
Increase the cost of one repair from 1 part to 2 parts.

## Tuning Knob Mapping
| Knob | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| repair_cost | 1 | 2 |

## Acceptance Criteria
- With three parts, a valid repair consumes two and leaves one.
- With fewer than two parts, a repair consumes nothing and the lamp remains faulty.

## Approval
The scripted fixture user explicitly authorizes this quick spec and the described change to repair.md. No change to parts.md, the entity registry or ADR is authorized; their owners must review the impact first.

# Game Brief: Beacon Keeper

**One-sentence pitch:** Repair a storm-battered lighthouse before the harbor closes.

## Core loop
- Inspect a damaged lamp, gather a part, repair the fault, then test the beam.

## Player goal & fail state — what working looks like
Restore the beacon before the storm clock expires; an unrepaired beacon at expiry fails the run.

## MVP — what must exist to be the game
- Lamp inspection and one visible fault.
- Part gathering and a repair interaction.
- Storm timer and a beam test.

## Out of scope — not building this
No multiplayer, procedural world or persistent inventory.

## Build order
1. Test the repair interaction and feedback before adding the storm clock.

**Who it's for / what they feel:** Solo puzzle players seeking calm tension.
**Art & audio direction:** Ink silhouettes, rain and muted coastal sounds.
**Reference game:** The Long Dark — retain weather pressure, not survival systems.

# Repair

> **Status**: In Design
> **Author**: scripted fixture user and in-session reviewer
> **Last Updated**: 2026-11-05
> **Last Verified**: 2026-11-05
> **Implements Pillar**: readable tactile repair puzzle

## Summary
The player spends two parts to repair the lighthouse lamp.

> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Core` · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `Parts`

## Overview
Inspect the faulty lamp, spend a part, then test the beacon before the storm expires.

## Detailed Design
### Core Rules
A repair consumes exactly two parts and restores one fault; a working lamp cannot consume parts.
### States and Transitions
Faulty -> repaired after a successful repair; repaired -> tested after the beacon test.
### Interactions with Other Systems
Parts supplies the resource and must refuse a repair if none is available.

## Formulas
parts_after = parts_before - 2 when a valid repair occurs. parts_before is an integer >= 2; parts_after is an integer >= 0. Example: 3 becomes 1.

## Edge Cases
Fewer than two parts: do not change state or count. Already repaired: do not spend a part.

## Dependencies
Depends on Parts; Parts lists Repair as a dependent.

## Visual/Audio Requirements
Use an obvious lamp-state indicator; final art and sound are not yet specified.

## Game Feel
A repair should communicate completion; timing awaits playtest.

## UI Requirements
Show a readable count and whether the lamp is repaired.

## Cross-References
Parts: parts.md (resource count and consumption).

## Acceptance Criteria
- With 3 parts and a fault, repair leaves 1 part and the lamp repaired.
- With fewer than 2 parts, repair leaves the count and lamp state unchanged.
- A second repair on a repaired lamp spends no parts.

## Open Questions
Animation duration awaits user design choice.
